why: A pacemaker steered by rising light, gated by a dark detector. Wall, adaptation (S1-S3) and comparator (F, SL at bias -5.2) as design 4. D is a near-critical switch (self 4.3, bias -5.54) on the wall's front-blind sum: off at night (sum ~3.25), on from light ~0.045 (sum ~3.43), so the cell rests at night as B8 does. With D on, R (self 5, bias -4) and its timer Q (tau 30, driven 4.5 by R, bias -4) form a pacemaker: R fires a burst (front half beats), Q rises and ends it after ~8 ticks, Q decays and R fires again after ~56 ticks (duty ~12%, B5's exploring runs built in). F - SL shifts R's input: after a burst that raised the light, R fires again sooner (in the far field about twice as soon); after one that lowered it, R stays quiet until SL forgets. B5's run-while-rising, as a pace that speeds up going uphill and stops going downhill. No bright-light gate: near the mouth the cell hops and stays, since hops away lower the light.
